Subject: CAIQ: targeted 3rd-party dependency scan cadence & exception log

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for taking this. As part of Acme's CAIQ review we need a concise packet describing how Redwood handles third-party dependency scanning (runtime libs, container base images, and infra dependencies) and the exception/compensating-controls workflow when a vendor library is marked "unfixable" or requires a vendor patch. Specifically can you provide: 

- The cadence of SBOM/OSS dependency scans and full infra vulnerability scans (how often, what scope)
- SLA targets for critical/high CVEs (detection -> fix/mitigation)
- The exception approval path and required approvals for production-impacting dependencies
- A sample exception log (last 90 days) and any attestation that the CISO can sign confirming adherence to the SLA for critical CVEs

If possible, please attach a CSV export of the most recent third-party-dependency scan plus any exception log. We have a CAIQ slot next week and need material by Monday EOD PT.

Appreciate it — Paul
Paul Nguyen
Security Engineer, Acme Corp
security@acme-corp.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: CAIQ: targeted 3rd-party dependency scan cadence & exception log

Paul —

Thanks for the clear ask. High level summary below; I've attached a CSV export and an exception spreadsheet as requested. If you want a single-slide summary for CAIQ, say the word and I can produce it.

Summary of Redwood's third-party dependency scanning and exception procedure:

- Cadence & scope:
  - SBOM-derived dependency scans: nightly (automated) against public CVE databases + vendor advisories; we produce per-service CSV output.
  - Container base-image & infra full scans: weekly for production clusters; daily for canary/beta clusters.
  - Monthly end-to-end pentest-derived package audits for host-level and infra components.

- SLA targets:
  - Critical (CVSS >=9): initial triage within 24 hours; mitigation or compensating control within 7 calendar days (we document workarounds if vendor patching is required).
  - High (CVSS 7-8.9): triage within 3 business days; mitigation/patch within 30 calendar days unless an exception is granted.
  - Medium/low: prioritized by risk-based scoring and backlog grooming.

- Exception & approvals workflow:
  - Exception requests created in the vulnerability tracker with required fields (impact assessment, mitigation plan, compensating controls).
  - Approval chain: Service Owner -> Security Engineering -> CISO (for exceptions >60 days or for critical components).
  - Exceptions are logged in a centralized spreadsheet (attached) and surfaced weekly to the SRE/Platform leads.

- Evidence included (attachments):
  - thirdparty-dep-scan-summary-20260730.csv (export from dependency scanner showing vendor packages, CVEs, severity, infra tag, and suggested remediations)
  - cve-exception-log-20260730.xlsx (exception tracker with approvals, rationale, compensating controls)

I'll also ask Soojin and Rafael to add a short attestation text from security leadership you can include in your CAIQ packet. If you need CVE-level evidence for the last 3 critical closures (audit trail, PRs, deploy notes), I can bundle that; it will be a small zip (we keep those available).

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0132

Thanks Kimberly — that is helpful. Two follow-ups before I slot this in the CAIQ doc: 

1) Can you provide the exception approval timestamps (who approved and when) for the three oldest open exceptions in the log? We need the audit trail plus links to PRs or mitigation tickets where applicable.
2) For the most recent three critical CVEs you closed in production, can you provide an evidence pack (audit log of deploys, PR links, ticket numbers)? In CAIQ we mark "closed incidents" and auditors want the chain of custody.

Also, we require a short signed attestation from your security leadership that the 7-day SLA for critical CVEs is current practice. A plain-text attestation that we can include in the CAIQ is acceptable; if CISO prefers DocuSign that also works.

Can you confirm by EOD PT Monday? If not, please propose a ship date.

- Paul
